Drama
Drama
Achieve Arts Speech and Drama School are one of the top LAMDA providers in North London who deliver weekly LAMDA classes to Annemount pupils in Reception, Year One and Two. In the weekly drama sessions, the specialist teacher works on important life skills such as vocal projection, vocal diction, confidence building, concentration skills, improvisation, script work and performing arts skills.
Achieve Arts are registered as a private centre with LAMDA and they have a 100% success rate in all LAMDA examinations. The team are highly experienced, having all trained at accredited Drama Schools and they work on LAMDA graded material with our students.
The teacher works on Introductory and Entry Level LAMDA material and when Year One and Two pupils are ready, each student is nominated for their LAMDA exam. It is a wonderful accomplishment and each student feels proud of themselves and it is a huge confidence building experience.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Private Education in London | Annemount School
pageCache.text:
Music
Music
Music is part of the curriculum and children learn to sing and use different instruments (as well as make their own) to make music together and practise rhythm and pitch. Each day the pupils are welcomed with music as they go about their morning preparations. The benefits of music include improved memory and focus as well as feeling good!
Each term, the school focuses on a classical composer, such as Bach, or a genre of music, such as Latin American.
All of our Early Years pupils have regular music and movement sessions. These uplift, energise and encourage optimum physical development. Singing is encouraged daily, a wonderful addition to wellbeing as well as aiding memory and developing language skills through rhyme. Individual Singing Lessons, Piano as well as Violin can begin from the earliest age at Annemount. Dance is offered to all pupils in which music and rhythm are a feature.
Singing and music, including drumming and dance, are integral to the curriculum. Year One and Year Two pupils also learn the recorder and music notation (theory). All of these sessions are taught by specialist teachers.
Violin is taught to a high standard by a specialist teacher. About a third of the pupils take up this option and motivate each other. The sessions develop coordination and concentration, good posture, confidence and memory skills, self-correction, multi-tasking and sequencing as well as self-discipline. There is an endless list of ways as to how learning an instrument contributes to general study skills. Most importantly, the programme of study instils the importance of practice and patience to gain mastery, a valuable life skill.
Our Choir performs at local residential homes and Great Ormond Street Hospital.
Annemount offers many performance opportunities throughout the school year and in the summer there is a dedicated violin concert with special guest players amongst former pupils, adding to the programme and accentuating the progress that is made over time.

Nursery & Pre-Reception
Nursery & Pre-Reception
Preparing for 4+, Annemount’s Nursery and Pre-Reception programme offers a nurturing, varied and fun-filled early years experience in Hampstead Garden Suburb. As an independent school, we ensure children feel safe and loved as they begin their educational journey, developing confidence and independence. The focus of our curriculum is to instil curiosity and a love of learning.
Children are eligible to start Annemount when they are aged two. The school offers the parents flexibility with options of mornings, extended mornings and lunch until 1pm, or full days up until 5pm.
The Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum includes all seven areas of learning: Communication and Language, Physical Development, Literacy, Maths, Understanding the World, Expressive Arts and Design and Personal, Social and Emotional Development. The children benefit from specialist led sessions in Music, Dance and Mini Kickers Football. Older Nursery pupils have the opportunity to begin Violin lessons.
The children learn to become a considerate member of the class community and to think, enquire, anticipate, process and make sense of the world around them. Their lessons are enriched with stories, poetry, singing, arts and crafts, circle-time and creative play with a balance of practical activities and directed learning.
The youngest pupils have their own dedicated garden where the children explore, play, learn and even do some gardening! Each day, time is spent outdoors engaging in activities such as nature investigation, sport and team games.
Our pupils are well-rounded and well-prepared for Reception and 4+.

pageCache.text:
PTA Community
PTA Community
Enhancing school life for Annemount pupils:
The PTA organises several activities for the children, including visits from a farm, various workshops to support specific initiatives within the school such as dedicated Science or Maths weeks, and of course, the magnificent Summer Fete.
Enhancing school life for Annemount parents:
The PTA provides a forum for parents to get to know each other and to share information. We host a great year of social events both in and out of school including coffee mornings with the Head. The PTA also assists with school events such as Parent Education Talks and Open Days.
Raising money for charity:
The PTA is also heavily focused on raising money for local and national charities relating to children.
PTA meetings are a great way to get involved and meet other parents. The PTA relies on volunteers and good ideas, as well as a willingness to participate in some small way such as simply baking a cake for the Bake Sale!
The school supports Food Bank Aid in North Finchley. On the first Friday of each month, the school hosts a collection for the charity. Our Year Two ‘Food Bankers’ delivery the donations direct to the food bank and help to sort the items.

Dance
Dance
All pupils have their Dance sessions as part of the curriculum.
Initially the pupils learn general Music and Movement. They develop listening, sequencing and coordination skills as well as an understanding of spatial awareness before they graduate into more formal dancing.
Year One and Year Two pupils explore the beginnings of choreography, expressing life experiences through Dance. They also acquire knowledge of basic balletic steps which are the foundation of the first Primary examination.

Computing
Computing
Reception children work on mastering their mouse skills, using the keyboard, creating pictures and saving, simple sequencing and testing algorithms alongside a wide variety of educational Apps that support the Early Years Foundation Stage.
In Year One the children begin to edit text in Word, use the file menu to manage documents, explore windows and learn all about algorithms/creating code to make things happen!
Year Two progress by building and coding a mini computer, programming interactive robots and creating amazing animations using Scratch and other similar apps. In addition they learn all about the internet and email, and how to stay safe online.
The school is committed to working with parents to inform them of current developments regarding internet safety.
Take a look at this helpful website for more information.

Foreign Language
French or Spanish is taught from Reception as part of the curriculum.
The lessons are taught creatively with a variety of resources focussing on different topics developing listening and memory skills as well as confidence with speaking and communication.
Songs are also used extensively to enhance the enjoyment of learning a new language.
The main purpose of the lessons is to spark their interest in other modern languages going forward.
